results.title: 📈 Democrats recover their generic ballot edge

results.content:
Three out of four voters questioned in the most recent Fox News national poll said inflation had caused financial hardship, while 54% expected the economy to worsen.

The Fox News poll and other recent surveys also indicate Democrats holding an enthusiasm advantage over Republicans, and continuing to lead on the generic ballot question, which asks if a respondent would vote for the Democrat or Republican in their congressional district without offering specific names.
results.title: Johnson downplays GOP's midterm woes as Democrats eye House takeover: 'I am very bullish'

results.content:
According to recent Emerson College polling, 51% of voters support the Democratic candidate on a generic ballot. A Reuters/Ipsos poll shows that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate, versus 37% who would vote Republican.

These are signs the party is on the mend. And although Democrats could be doing even better if the party had been campaigning throughout the past two years, now is not the time to stop caring.
